note: inferred: leaves London in the Resolution with the Discovery, Captain John Ingram; no exact day is recorded
inferred: anchors at the Digges Islands as instructed and assembles a pinnace; five men are killed here
inferred: falls in with the west shore of the bay in about 60 deg 40 min and names it Hopes Checked, the first European crossing of Hudson Bay
takes harbour in Port Nelson and names the river for his sailing master Nelson, whom he buried there; Pricket gives the 13th and Button's own board says the 27th
the river finally freezes over, after several thaws; Button had been sick all winter and began to mend on 24 January
the ice clears from the river; many men are dead and the Resolution has to be abandoned
back off Hopes Checked; from here the only account is Sir Thomas Roe's abstract of Button's lost journal
inferred: names Hopes Advance, somewhere on the north-west shore; the identification is uncertain
his farthest north, about 65 deg, in the strait later named Sir Thomas Roe's Welcome; marked Ne Ultra on the old charts
inferred: down the west side of Southampton Island and back to the west end of Hudson Strait to work the tides
inferred: home by the passage since called Button's Isles, near Cape Chidley, rather than the main channel
inferred: in England by 27 September, when Phineas Pett records Button alighting at his house newly returned
